title: AI assistants in daily work
intro: Some people use AI tools every day to save time, while others worry this can reduce independent thinking.
prompt: What about you: do AI tools usually make your work easier, or more confusing?

title: Using AI for writing
intro: Many people use AI to draft emails and documents, but some worry the tone becomes generic.
prompt: When you write with AI, what part feels most useful and what part still needs your own touch?

title: Trust in AI answers
intro: AI can answer quickly, but quick answers are not always correct.
prompt: How do you decide when to trust an AI answer and when to double-check?

title: Learning with AI
intro: Some learners feel AI gives confidence, while others feel overwhelmed by too many suggestions.
prompt: In your learning process, does AI reduce stress or increase stress? Why?

title: Speed vs quality
intro: AI can speed up first drafts, but final quality still depends on human review.
prompt: In your experience, where should you slow down even when AI helps you go faster?

title: When AI gets your intent wrong
intro: Sometimes AI output is fluent but misses what you actually mean.
prompt: What signals tell you that AI misunderstood your intent?

title: Adopting AI tools
intro: Teams often debate whether to use one AI tool deeply or many tools lightly.
prompt: If you had to choose one approach, which would you pick and why?

title: Prompt clarity
intro: A small change in prompt wording can produce very different results.
prompt: What is one habit that helps you write clearer prompts?

title: Feeling uneasy about AI
intro: People can see AI benefits and still feel uneasy about long-term impact.
prompt: Do you feel more hopeful or more uneasy about AI recently? What changed?

title: AI and meeting notes
intro: AI summaries can save time after meetings, but details may be lost.
prompt: Would you rather have a shorter summary or a more detailed one? Why?

title: AI in personal planning
intro: Some people use AI to plan their week, while others prefer manual planning.
prompt: Do you use AI to plan your tasks, or do you prefer your own system?

title: AI and originality
intro: A common concern is that heavy AI use might make ideas less original.
prompt: How do you keep your own voice when AI helps you draft content?

title: Tool overload
intro: Too many AI tools can create friction instead of saving time.
prompt: What is one sign that your AI workflow is getting too complicated?

title: Choosing what to automate
intro: Not every task should be automated, even if it can be automated.
prompt: Which type of task do you refuse to automate, and why?

title: Getting unstuck
intro: When you are stuck, AI can provide options quickly, but too many options can distract you.
prompt: When you ask AI for help, do you prefer one suggestion or multiple options?

title: AI in product thinking
intro: AI can help generate feature ideas, but not all ideas fit real user needs.
prompt: How do you filter AI-generated ideas before turning them into real product decisions?

title: AI regulation
intro: Some people want stricter AI rules for safety, while others worry regulation will slow innovation.
prompt: Where do you stand between safety and speed, and why?

title: Confidence in English with AI
intro: AI feedback can help language learners speak more confidently, but it can also create dependence.
prompt: Do AI tools make you more independent or more dependent in language learning?

title: AI recommendations
intro: Recommendation systems can save search time, but they may narrow your perspective.
prompt: Have AI recommendations helped you discover better content, or trapped you in repetition?

title: Human judgment
intro: Even with strong AI assistance, human judgment still matters in ambiguous situations.
prompt: What decision types should always remain human-led, in your opinion?
